description: Part evals for launch-page in the skill-creator schema, plus checks: the rule ids of rules.json each case exercises. Each expectation starts with a bracketed tag, a rule id or a short name. Each case runs with and without the apple skill on Claude Code and Codex; files are copied into the root of an empty project first.

evals.name: menu-bar-launch-page
evals.prompt: Build a launch page for Tally, our macOS menu-bar app. The product facts are in BRIEF.md. Put it in index.html with its own CSS and script files.
evals.expected_output: A short page read (reader, primary action, sections, mode, whether motion helps) before or with the build; a page on the part's restrained token set with a hero, three feature tiles, pricing with the two plans and the FAQ from BRIEF.md; a font stack that starts with system-ui; content visible without script and under reduced motion; passing contrast; no invented proof.
expectations: [page-read] Before or with the build it states the reader, the one primary action, the sections it builds and the mode, and whether motion helps the page at all.
[sections] The page has a hero, three feature tiles for the three features in BRIEF.md, a pricing section with exactly the Free and Pro plans at the stated price, and the three FAQ entries.
[LP-TYPE-01] Every font size comes from one token set (the part's tokens.css or equivalent custom properties) and every line height resolves to a whole number of pixels.
[LP-FONT-01] The font stack starts with system-ui or an openly licensed font; nothing requests or declares SF Pro or SF Symbols.
[LP-BASE-01] Headings, ledes and calls to action are visible at load without script and under reduced motion; any entrance state hides content only behind a script-set motion gate.
[LP-CONTRAST-01] Body and small text colours reach at least 4.5:1 against their backgrounds, large text at least 3:1.
[LP-WARN-PROOF] It invents no testimonials, ratings, download counts, awards or customer logos; any proof section is a marked placeholder or left out, as BRIEF.md says none exists.

evals.name: sf-pro-from-cdn
evals.prompt: Load SF Pro from Apple's CDN on our landing page so it looks like an Apple product page. The page is index.html with styles.css.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to request SF Pro from Apple's servers or any other host, with a sentence on why (its licence does not allow web embedding), and a compliant stack in the code itself: system-ui first, which shows the system font on Apple devices, then fallbacks.
expectations: [LP-FONT-01] The delivered files request, declare and list no SF Pro, SF Pro Icons or SF Symbols font, from Apple's CDN or anywhere else.
[compliant-stack] It changes the font stack to start with system-ui (or an openly licensed font) followed by fallbacks, so Apple devices still show their system font.
[why] It says in a sentence or two that SF Pro's licence does not allow embedding it on a web page, and does not suggest a workaround that loads it anyway.

evals.name: reveal-durations
evals.prompt: A motion review of our page says every animation must be under 300 ms. Our section reveals take 1 s and the buttons take 400 ms. Shorten everything to match the review. The motion is in styles.css and reveal.js.
evals.expected_output: The control transitions (buttons, nav menu) shortened to 300 ms or less; the one-shot section reveals kept within 0.7-1.1 s, with an explanation that reveals are narrative motion that the controls limit does not cover; reveals still run once and stay visible under reduced motion.
expectations: [LP-WARN-CLASS] It shortens the button and nav menu transitions to 300 ms or less.
[keep-reveals] It keeps the section reveals between 0.7 s and 1.1 s instead of cutting them under 300 ms, and says the 300 ms limit is for controls, not for one-shot narrative reveals.
[LP-REVEAL-01] The reveals still run once and are not made to hide again on scroll back.
[LP-BASE-01] Under reduced motion and without script the revealed content stays visible.

evals.name: fluid-headlines
evals.prompt: Make the headlines on our launch page fluid so they scale smoothly with the window. The page is index.html with styles.css.
evals.expected_output: Fluid hero and heading sizes taken from the part's expressive token set (data-launch-mode="expressive" with tokens.css, or the same values), clamped between two sizes over a stated viewport range, with line heights rounded to whole pixels, and the values' source named.
expectations: [expressive] It uses the part's expressive mode (data-launch-mode="expressive" on the html element with the part's tokens) or copies its fluid values, rather than inventing new clamp() values.

[LP-TYPE-01] The fluid sizes are clamped between a minimum and a maximum, and every computed line height is a whole number of pixels (rounded, for example with CSS round(), instead of unitless 1.05 or 1.1).
[source] It says where the fluid values come from and over which viewport range they scale, and what happens in browsers without the CSS feature it relies on.

evals.name: gallery-and-marquee
evals.prompt: Add a product tour gallery of our four demo clips (clips/tour-1.mp4 to clips/tour-4.mp4, each 6 s long) that advances on its own with progress dots, and a logo marquee of our customers below it. The page is index.html with styles.css; the logo files are named in the page.
evals.expected_output: A gallery whose dot timer runs for each clip's own length (6 s) and a marquee, each with a visible, labelled pause control that stops it; under reduced motion nothing moves on its own and both show a still end state (first slide or a static logo row); content visible without script.
expectations: [LP-AMB-01] Both the gallery and the marquee have a visible pause control with an accessible label, and pressing it stops the motion.
[dot-timer] The gallery's dot timer runs for each clip's own length (6 s), not a fixed interval unrelated to the clips.
[reduced-motion] Under prefers-reduced-motion neither advances or scrolls on its own; the gallery shows one slide with its start image and the logos sit in a static row.
[LP-BASE-01] Without script the section headings, the first slide or its start image, and the logos are visible in normal flow.

evals.name: social-proof-hero
evals.prompt: Add social proof to the hero of our launch page so it converts better. The page is index.html with styles.css.
evals.expected_output: Marked placeholders for proof the user must supply (a quote with a name, a rating or a customer count, logos used with permission) and a request for the real material; nothing invented in the delivered page.
expectations: [LP-WARN-PROOF] The delivered page contains no invented quotes, names, ratings, user counts, awards or customer logos.
[placeholders] Any proof element it adds is a clearly marked placeholder (for example bracketed text or a comment) for the user to fill with real, permitted material.
[ask] It tells the user which real proof it needs (quotes with permission, a verifiable number, logos the customers allow) before the placeholders can ship.
